name: Fatal Infantile Encephalopathy-Pulmonary Hypertension Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Fatal Infantile Encephalopathy-Pulmonary Hypertension Syndrome

criteria.description: Progressive severe infantile encephalopathy with developmental regression
Evidence of pulmonary arterial hypertension confirmed by echocardiography or cardiac catheterization
Onset of neurological and respiratory symptoms within the first year of life
Exclusion of other metabolic, infectious, or genetic causes of encephalopathy and pulmonary hypertension
Brain MRI showing diffuse cerebral atrophy and white matter abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria (progressive infantile encephalopathy, confirmed pulmonary hypertension, and early onset) plus exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but no specific gene identified yet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive infantile encephalopathy with developmental regression
pathognomonic.notes: Rapid neurological decline typically within months
searchTerms: infant brain disease with loss of skills
progressive brain dysfunction with skill loss

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pulmonary arterial hypertension confirmed by echocardiography
pathognomonic.notes: Elevated pulmonary artery pressures causing respiratory distress
searchTerms: high blood pressure in lungs confirmed by echo
increased lung artery pressure on echocardiogram

pathognomonic.notes: Marked muscle weakness and reduced tone

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulties with failure to thrive
common.notes: Poor oral intake and growth retardation
searchTerms: difficulty eating causing failure to thrive

common.notes: Increased work of breathing secondary to pulmonary hypertension
Generalized or focal seizures may occur
Delayed acquisition of motor and cognitive milestones

occasional.notes: Enlarged liver due to right heart failure
Swelling due to right heart failure

laboratory: Normal metabolic screening excluding other causes
Mild hypoxemia on arterial blood gas
imaging: Brain MRI showing diffuse cerebral atrophy and white matter abnormalities
Echocardiography demonstrating elevated pulmonary artery pressures
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and pulmonary vascular congestion
genetic: No specific gene identified; genetic testing to exclude other metabolic or mitochondrial disorders
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing diffuse slowing consistent with encephalopathy

distinguishingFeatures: Multi-organ involvement beyond brain and lungs

redFlags: Rapid neurological deterioration within first year of life
Severe pulmonary hypertension refractory to standard therapies
Failure to thrive with combined neurological and respiratory symptoms
references: Orphanet: Fatal infantile encephalopathy-pulmonary hypertension syndrome (ORPHA:293838)
